rationale: The working diagnosis identified the lack of evidence for direct willingness to pay, security procurement and channel alignment as the concentrated limiter. Version 4 therefore stops treating each regulated entity as the initial payer and makes a DORA advisor or managed-service provider the hypothesized payer and prime contractor, with a white-label customer-controlled runtime priced per partner, active entity or reporting cycle while the partner retains remediation revenue. This changes the customer, payer, distribution, offer, control point, critical dependency, capital need, founder time, pricing and wealth-path economics rather than merely changing copy. It does not claim a partner commitment, client permission, willingness to pay, security acceptance, lead flow, margin or renewal; free official tooling, regulator training, first-cycle learning, incumbent competition and sensitive-data constraints remain explicit.
